newsitem.title: CANADA: Pools drop UGG bid after judge's ruling.
newsitem.headline: Pools drop UGG bid after judge's ruling.

text.p: United Grain Growers Ltd Chief Executive Officer Brian Hayward said on Tuesday that a C$172 million hostile takeover bid for his firm by two rival grainhandlers was dropped at 1310 Central Time (1410 EST/1910 GMT).
"At noon Central (Time) we got the judge's decision and at about 1:10 Central we were advised simultaneously by the Pools' legal counsel they were dropping the bid," Hayward told Reuters.
Privately held Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators on February 20 launched at C$13.75 a share hostile bid for UGG, one of Canada's largest grain handlers.

"I have concluded that as a result of the pre-tender agreement with Lindner, the Pools became the beneficial owner, within the meaning of the plan, of Lindner shares. All shares beneficially owned by the Pools are subject to the consequences of the triggering of the poison pill," Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench Justice John Scollin said in his written ruling.

AWP and MPE made a C$172 million hostile takeover bid for UGG Feb 20 when they announced an irrevokable lock-up agreement with U.S. mutual fund Lindner Growth Fund for 6.4 percent of shares in addition to the 14.98 percent they owned.
AWP chief financial officer Geoff Southwood was not immediately available for comment but planned a conference call for 1530 EST/2030 GMT. MPE's president was not available.

UGG's board of directors adopted a shareholder rights plan Feb 14 granting any shareholder other than a hostile bidder the option to purchase 8.5 more shares for each one already held at C$5.88 each. The plan could be triggered once any one shareholder acquired 15 percent or more of UGG stock.
More than 19 million new limited common voting shares in UGG would be added to the market if all eligible shareholders opt to buy more stock, a Pool consultant has said.
"The Board will be meeting shortly to consider setting the separation time for the rights issued under the Plan after which the rights will be exercisable," a UGG statement said.
UGG's board will consider actions it may take to assist shareholders who may lack the financing to acquire more UGG shares through the rights plan, UGG said.
"The rights plan was put in place to protect our shareholders against an unfair creeping takeover such as this one," said UGG president Ted Allen said in the statement.
"The Pools knew the details of our Plan before they launched this hostile takeover," Allen added.
